name: Question 5
problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14094870/assets/f7232aba64209d02a92806df522484a1e233b4ad083bd2479a4e9bfabd7b3e63.png)

A plate of mass $M$ occupies region bounded by two circles ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=1$ and ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=4$ and two lines $y=x$ and $y=-x$ in the first and second quadrant, as shown above. Its mass density at any point is given by $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{M\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}{2{y}^{2}}.$ Find the radius of gyration of the plate about the $x$-axis.
worked_solution:
For a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ with mass $M$ and mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{x}$ about the $x$-axis is given by
${R}_{x}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{x}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{x}$ is the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{y}$ about the $y$-axis is given by
${R}_{y}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{y}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{y}$ is the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{0}$ about the origin is given by
${R}_{0}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{0}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{0}$ is the moment of inertia about the origin.

In polar coordinates, the region occupied by the plate is given by

$$
D={(r,\theta )\,:\,1\le r\le 2,\,\,\frac{\pi }{4}\le \theta \le \frac{3\pi }{4}}.
$$

The moment of inertia about the $x$-axis, in polar coordinates, is defined as

$$
{I}_{x}={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta ){r}^{3}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta ,
$$

where $\lambda (r,\theta )$ is the mass density function.

Also, the mass density in terms of polar coordinates is $\lambda (r,\theta )=\frac{M}{2r{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }.$
Therefore, the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{x} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta ){r}^{3}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{M}{2}{\int }_{\pi /4}^{3\pi /4}{\int }_{1}^{2}{r}^{2}\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{M}{2}({\int }_{1}^{2}{r}^{2}\,\text{d}r)({\int }_{\pi /4}^{3\pi /4}\,\text{d}\theta ) \\  & =\frac{M}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{3}{r}^{3}{|}_{1}^{2}\cdot \theta {|}_{\pi /4}^{3\pi /4} \\  & =\frac{M}{2}\cdot \frac{7}{3}\cdot \frac{\pi }{2} \\  & =\frac{7\pi M}{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of gyration about the $x$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{x} & =\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{x}}{M}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{7\pi M}{12}\cdot \frac{1}{M}} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\frac{7\pi }{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5

A plate of mass M occupies region bounded by two circles x2+y2=1 and x2+y2=4 and two lines y=x and y=−x in the first and second quadrant, as shown above. Its mass density at any point is given by λ(x,y)=Mx2+y22y2. Find the radius of gyration of the plate about the x-axis.

a
 123π2
b
 35π2
c
 127π3
d
 5π6
e
 7π5
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a plane lamina in the shape of a region D with mass M and mass density function λ(x,y), we have the following definitions:

  • The radius of gyration Rx about the x-axis is given by Rx=IxM, where Ix is the moment of inertia about the x-axis.

  • The radius of gyration Ry about the y-axis is given by Ry=IyM, where Iy is the moment of inertia about the y-axis.

  • The radius of gyration R0 about the origin is given by R0=I0M, where I0 is the moment of inertia about the origin.

In polar coordinates, the region occupied by the plate is given by D={(r,θ):1≤r≤2,π4≤θ≤3π4}.

The moment of inertia about the x-axis, in polar coordinates, is defined as

Ix=∬Dλ(r,θ)r3sin2⁡θdrdθ,

where λ(r,θ) is the mass density function.

Also, the mass density in terms of polar coordinates is λ(r,θ)=M2rsin2⁡θ. Therefore, the moment of inertia about the y-axis is

Ix=∬Dλ(r,θ)r3sin2⁡θdrdθ=M2∫π/43π/4∫12r2drdθ=M2(∫12r2dr)(∫π/43π/4dθ)=M2⋅13r3|12⋅θ|π/43π/4=M2⋅73⋅π2=7πM12.

Therefore, the radius of gyration about the x-axis is

Rx=IxM=7πM12⋅1M=127π3.
